question: The product \((8)(888\dots8),\) where the second factor has \(k\) digits, is an integer whose digits have a sum of \(1000.\) What is \(k?\)
solution:
The repeated digits make column multiplication useful: once the same carry repeats, all the remaining columns behave alike. If \(k=1\), the product is \(64\), whose digit sum is only \(10\), so we need \(k\geq2\).

Starting at the right, \(8\cdot8=64\), so the units digit is \(4\) and the carry is \(6\). The next column gives \(8\cdot8+6=70\), so its digit is \(0\) and the carry is \(7\). Every remaining column gives \(8\cdot8+7=71\), writing a \(1\) and again carrying \(7\). After the last column, that carry becomes the leading digit.

Thus the product has a leading \(7\), followed by \(k-2\) ones, and then the digits \(04\). This also covers \(k=2\), when there are no ones and the product is \(704\). Its digit sum is therefore
\[
7+(k-2)+0+4=k+9.
\]
Setting this equal to \(1000\) gives \(k=991\), which satisfies \(k\geq2\). The answer is \(\boxed{991}\), choice D.
